questions.q: What does IDENTITY(1,1) do on a column?
options: Auto-increments the column starting at 1, by 1, on every successful INSERT
Requires every INSERT to manually supply a unique value
Makes the column allow NULL values
Automatically creates a foreign key to another table
questions.explain: The first argument is the starting value, the second is the increment — SQL Server generates the value automatically on each INSERT.

questions.q: Why is SCOPE_IDENTITY() the recommended default for reading back a generated identity value?
options: It returns the last identity value from your current session and current scope, unaffected by triggers elsewhere
It's the only function that works at all
It returns the identity value for every table in the database at once
It automatically locks the table to prevent concurrent inserts
questions.explain: SCOPE_IDENTITY() is scoped to exactly the statement you ran, which is why it's safe even when other scopes or sessions are active.

questions.q: Why is @@IDENTITY considered a real footgun?
options: It returns the last identity value inserted in the current session across ANY scope, so a trigger's insert can silently clobber the value you wanted
It only works for IDENTITY(1,1), not other increment values
It requires a transaction to be open
It cannot be used in a SELECT statement
questions.explain: If a trigger on the table inserts into a different table, @@IDENTITY returns that trigger's value instead of yours.

questions.q: What does IDENT_CURRENT('table') return, and why is it the least safe for concurrent use?
options: The last identity value generated for that table across ANY session, which another user's concurrent insert could have produced
The next identity value that will be generated, before any INSERT runs
The first identity value ever inserted into the table
It is identical in behavior to SCOPE_IDENTITY()
questions.explain: Because it isn't scoped to your session at all, a concurrent insert by someone else can change what it returns.

questions.q: In a system with multiple users inserting into the same table at once, which identity function should you trust to get YOUR row's generated ID?
options: SCOPE_IDENTITY()
@@IDENTITY
IDENT_CURRENT('table')
Any of the three — they always return the same value
questions.explain: Only SCOPE_IDENTITY() is scoped narrowly enough to guarantee it reflects your own INSERT, not a trigger's or another session's.
